items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I had heard of Hank Jones but not met him.

ctx.x: The trumpet player had a style that seemed to be a mixture of Charlie Shavers and Howard McGee but it was not as hard as Charlie's and he had plenty of feeling and ideas galore. After about two hours of jamming by Facey and his fine trumpet player, I was able to get

into a conversation with the latter. He told me that his name was Thad Jones, and his brother was Hank Jones, the piano man. I had heard of Hank Jones but not met him. Hank had the reputation o being a fine accompanist and a great soloist. I later discovered that the reputation of Hank was not a conjectural narrative but a comformity.

Thad told me that he and Facey were in a U.S. army show that Thad had arranged all the music for. I had the feeling that Thad was going places after he would be discharged from the army and a few years later, that premonition came true. That cat played too much horn at that time to not have been better known than he was,.
